battle.name: 阿魯斯圖克戰爭
battle.theater: 緬因州北部阿魯斯圖克河谷
battle.brief: 一八三八年十二月三十一日，卡里布附近新不倫瑞克伐木工與緬因民兵因黑熊引發的誤射短兵相接，糾紛升至一八三九年二月，緬因州武裝團進駐阿魯斯圖克河、雙方互扣人質，卻始終未交戰，最後以一八四二年韋伯斯特—阿什伯頓條約劃界。卡面火繩槍早已退出戰列，民兵手中是燧發步槍。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 這場衝突的一方是美國緬因州及其聯邦政府，另一方是英國的新不倫瑞克殖民地與英屬北美。緬因方面以州權力主導：一八三六年州議會在爭議地做特別人口普查，普查代表埃比尼澤·格里利深入上阿魯斯圖克河谷後被新不倫瑞克總督約翰·哈維下令逮捕；州長羅伯特·鄧拉普隨即發布總動員令，宣稱有外國勢力入侵本州，州議會撥出八十萬美元的軍費，聯邦政府則授權總統召集民兵並撥給一千萬美元的預算。實際出動的是由州土地代理人魯弗斯·麥金泰爾、彭斯科特縣治安官與義勇民兵組成的武裝團，以及二月初從班戈爾出發的一支隊伍；主要將領有少將艾薩克·霍奇森，被授權率一千名志願者增援，另有聯邦準將溫菲爾德·斯科特於三月初抵達波士頓，主持了所謂「停戰管理」的安排。英方以新不倫瑞克為中心：總督哈維掌握殖民地民兵，並在伍德斯托克的軍械庫被伐木工奪用後發出動員；英國正規軍方面，由魁北克出發的第十一步兵團（德文郡團）四個連進駐此地，準備在聖約翰河對岸修建營房，新不倫瑞克又在流入阿魯斯圖克地區的各條支流上分兵駐守。新斯科舍則在議會中撥出一十萬美元支援新不倫瑞克。兩國中央層面的主角是美國總統馬丁·范布倫、國務卿丹尼爾·韋伯斯特與英方的阿什伯頓勛爵，談判最終在華盛頓完成。
countriesEn: One side was the state of Maine together with the federal government of the United States, the other the British colony of New Brunswick and British North America. The Maine side led the affair through the power of the state: in 1836 the legislature ordered a special census of the disputed country, and its representative Ebenezer Greeley was arrested in the upper Aroostook valley on the orders of the Governor of New Brunswick, John Harvey; Governor Robert Dunlap answered with a general order announcing that a foreign power had invaded Maine, the legislature voted 800,000 dollars for military defence, and the federal government authorised the President to call out the militia with ten million dollars. What actually moved was an armed posse made up of the state land agent Rufus McIntire, the sheriff of Penobscot County and volunteer militia, followed by a column that marched out of Bangor in early February. The commanders were Major General Isaac Hodsdon, authorised on 15 February to lead a thousand additional volunteers, and the federal brigadier Winfield Scott, who reached Boston in early March and arranged the administration of the so-called truce. The British side centred on New Brunswick: Governor Harvey controlled the colonial militia, and after the arsenal at Woodstock was broken into by lumbermen he called out the population; from the regular army four companies of the 11th (Devonshire) Regiment of Foot marched down from Quebec City to represent Canada and to build barracks across the Saint John River from Fort Kent, while New Brunswick posted regulars and militia on every tributary of the Saint John that flowed through the Aroostook country. Nova Scotia voted 100,000 dollars to support New Brunswick. At the level of the two central governments the actors were President Martin Van Buren, Secretary of State Daniel Webster and Lord Ashburton for Britain, and the settlement was concluded at Washington.
people: 推動這場「戰爭」的多半不是將軍而是文官。英方總督約翰·哈維是關鍵人物：他在未得倫敦指示的情況下先發制人，下令逮捕緬因州的普查代表，又以書信指控緬因州長受賄，聲稱若緬因繼續在阿魯斯圖克河流域行使司法便要動用武力，最後把雙方的扣押人質都當作「政治犯」處理，並把緬因方面的武力驅逐要求寫成正式公文送到華盛頓。緬因方面，州土地代理人魯弗斯·麥金泰爾與彭斯科特縣治安官率武裝團進入爭議地，在聖克魯瓦溪與阿魯斯圖克河交會處紮營，沒收新不倫瑞克伐木者的器具、逮捕伐木工送回州內受審；新不倫瑞克伐木工隨後破開伍德斯托克的軍械庫自行武裝，反過來把麥金泰爾一行用鎖鏈押回伍德斯托克扣押，接著雙方各扣對方指揮官，形成了「你扣我的人、我扣你的人」的荒誕局面。聯邦方面，總統馬丁·范布倫把準將溫菲爾德·斯科特派到衝突地，斯科特與哈維在1812年戰爭中曾有被俘與看管之誼，這層私人關係使雙方得以維持體面；斯科特建議緬因州五月與六月召回民兵，改以武裝民事團維持佔領，聯邦工程兵隨即著手興建福爾特菲爾德與福爾特肯特兩座要塞。國會方面，緬因州眾議員弗朗西斯·奧爾曼德·喬納森·史密斯在三月二日的辯論中陳述來龍去脈，主張本州若得不到聯邦回應便自行防衛；最後由國務卿韋伯斯特與英國特使阿什伯頓在華盛頓談成劃界條約。
peopleEn: Those who drove this war were mostly civilians rather than generals. On the British side Governor John Harvey was the pivot: acting before London had instructed him, he ordered the arrest of the Maine census taker, accused the Governor of Maine of bribery in writing, threatened military action if Maine continued to exercise jurisdiction in the basins of the Aroostook, and then treated the mutual arrests as the detention of political prisoners, while forwarding to Washington a formal demand that the Maine forces be withdrawn. On the Maine side the state land agent Rufus McIntire and the sheriff of Penobscot County led the armed posse into the disputed country, camped at the junction of the Saint Croix Stream and the Aroostook River, confiscated the New Brunswick lumbering equipment and arrested the woodcutters for trial in Maine; the New Brunswick lumbermen then broke into the arsenal at Woodstock, armed themselves, seized McIntire and his assistants in the middle of the night and carried them in chains to Woodstock, after which each side detained the other's commander, a neat impasse of arrests. On the federal side President Martin Van Buren sent Brigadier General Winfield Scott to the disputed area; Scott and Harvey had known each other from the War of 1812, when one was the other's prisoner and custodian, and that personal history allowed both to keep the matter dignified. Scott advised that the militia be recalled in May and June 1839 and replaced by an armed civil posse, and federal engineers began the permanent structures at Fort Fairfield and Fort Kent. In Congress, Representative Francis Ormond Jonathan Smith of Maine set out the whole history of the dispute in the debate of 2 March and argued that the state would defend its own territory if the national government would not; the settlement was finally made at Washington by Secretary of State Daniel Webster and the British envoy Lord Ashburton.
kits: 卡面這件火繩槍與這場衝突沒有可寫的交集，只能作為軍械沿革的底色。十六世紀的西班牙大方陣靠火繩槍的分排輪射形成彈幕，火繩槍的整套動作——點火、瞄準、列隊——在十九世紀初已完全被燧發槍與雷管槍取代，兩國軍械庫中殘存的火繩槍只是退役庫存，甚至被拿來教練新兵如何分排齊射。真正上陣的是民兵手上的滑膛槍：緬因民兵用美國一八一二年式的燧發滑膛步槍與逐步改裝的雷管式步槍，軍官配燧發手槍；英方殖民地民兵與正規第十一團同樣是燧發滑膛步槍，一八三五年起改用插座式刺刀，後膛仍是滑膛。砲方面，聯邦在霍爾敦的「漢考克營」駐紮第一砲兵團三個連，配可拆分的野戰砲與榴彈炮；英方沒有隨軍攻城重砲，靠的是新不倫瑞克沿聖約翰河各支流分置的民兵小分隊與地方警衛。木工與伐木者的裝備更為原始：鳥獵槍與斧頭，加上手斧與繩索，這些在卡里布衝突中就是實際上手的東西。工事方面，聯邦工程兵在一八三九年四月開始修築福爾特菲爾德，同年十月修築福爾特肯特，兩者都是土堤加木柵與碉樓的簡單堡壘，用來替代已經撤走的民兵。
kitsEn: The matchlock on this card has no real intersection with this conflict and can only serve as the base colour of a history of ordnance. The sixteenth-century Spanish square produced its volleys by firing the matchlock rank by rank, and the whole sequence the weapon demanded, lighting, aiming, forming ranks, had been completely replaced by the flintlock and the percussion cap in the early nineteenth century; the matchlocks left in the two countries' stores were retired stock, and were even used to drill new recruits in the discipline of firing by rank. What went into the field were the smoothbore muskets of the militia: the Maine militia used the American model 1812 flintlock smoothbore musket and smoothbores gradually converted to percussion, with flintlock pistols for officers; the New Brunswick militia and the regular 11th Foot likewise carried flintlock smoothbores, and the socket bayonet came in with the regulation of 1835, the chamber remaining smoothbore. On the artillery side, three companies of the 1st Artillery Regiment stood at Hancock Barracks near Houlton with field guns and howitzers that could be broken down for movement; the British brought no heavy siege artillery down, relying instead on the small militia detachments and country guards New Brunswick posted along the tributaries of the Saint John. The equipment of the woodcutters was far more primitive, hunting guns and axes with hand axes and rope, and it was these that were actually in hand during the clash at Caribou. On the works, federal engineers began Fort Fairfield in April 1839 and Fort Kent in October of the same year, both simple earth banks with stockades and blockhouses, built to take over from the militia that had been withdrawn.
tactics: 這場戰爭幾乎沒有會戰，因此戰術寫在部署與威懾上。英方的部署邏輯是守住河道與林權：總督哈維把阿魯斯圖克視為新不倫瑞克的一部分，命令各地武裝守住流入爭議區的各條支流，並在伍德斯托克儲存武器；美方的部署邏輯則是先派民事身分的人進場，試圖在對方警察抓到之前取得現場。一八三九年二月八日武裝團自班戈爾出發，走了數日後在聖克魯瓦溪與阿魯斯圖克河交會處紮營，沒收器具、扣押伐木工，此時新不倫瑞克方面破庫自取武器，反過來把美方的人用鎖鏈押走，接著兩邊各自扣住對方的軍事指揮官，僵局就這樣維持下去。真正改變局面的是聯邦的介入：斯科特到達後不再加派兵員，反而勸緬因州召回民兵，改由武裝民事團佔據，這一手法把軍事對峙降格為行政接管，同時由聯邦工程兵在兩處要點修築永久性要塞，英方則在對岸準備營房，兩軍相距一條河而不再相抵。卡里布的衝突本身則是一次誤會：十二月二十九日新不倫瑞克的伐木者在伊頓莊園舊址伐木，美方在莊園的家屬與武裝守衛前往驅逐，除夕夜雙方拔槍之際，一頭黑熊攻擊了加拿大伐木工，槍聲被當作對方開火而引發還擊，伐木工退出現場，此事經報紙渲染後才引出後面的扣人與出兵。
tacticsEn: Since this war produced almost no engagement, its tactics lie in deployment and intimidation. The British logic was to hold the rivers and the timber: Governor Harvey treated the Aroostook as part of New Brunswick, ordered the armed posts kept on every tributary running into the disputed country, and had weapons stored at Woodstock. The American logic was to get civilians on the ground first, to establish a presence before the other side's police could remove it. The posse marched out of Bangor on 8 February 1839, camped after several days at the junction of the Saint Croix Stream and the Aroostook River, and began confiscating equipment and arresting woodcutters for trial; the New Brunswick men then broke the Woodstock arsenal open, armed themselves, and carried the American officials away in chains, after which each side held the other's military commander and the impasse held. What actually changed the situation was the federal intervention: Scott, once on the ground, added no troops but advised Maine to recall the militia and hand the ground to an armed civil posse, which turned a military confrontation into an administrative takeover, while federal engineers raised permanent works at two points and the British prepared barracks across the river, the two forces no longer meeting but facing each other over a single river. The clash at Caribou itself was a misunderstanding: on 29 December New Brunswick woodcutters were felling timber on the old Eaton estate, the family and an armed guard on the American side went out to turn them off, and as both sides levelled their weapons on New Year's Eve a black bear charged the Canadian woodcutters; the shots were taken for an opening volley and answered, the woodcutters withdrew, and only after the press had made something of it did the arrests and the mobilisation follow.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。爭議的源頭是一七八三年《巴黎條約》未定清楚北界，一七九八年的聯合測量委員會只解決了聖克魯瓦河至奇普特內蒂庫湖一段；荷蘭國王威廉一世依一八三一年仲裁裁定美國得七千九百零八平方英里、英國得四千一百一十九平方英里，英國接受而緬因州拒絕，條約未能在美國國會通過。財政與授權方面，緬因州議會撥出八十萬美元，聯邦撥一千萬美元並授權總統召集民兵，國會休會期間另授權五十萬人的兵力，新斯科舍議會撥十萬美元。一八三九年一月二十四日緬因州議會授權州長派土地代理人、治安官與義勇民兵進剿，二月八日隊伍自班戈爾出發；二月十五日授權少將霍奇森率一千名志願者增援；二月十九日發布第七號總動員令；二月二十六日民兵連隊抵達上阿魯斯圖克並開始興建福爾特菲爾德。三月二日國會辯論，四月聯邦工程兵開始修築福爾特菲爾德，五月與六月民兵依斯科特建議撤回改由武裝民事團佔據，同年十月開始修築福爾特肯特。英方由魁北克調來第十一團四個連，聯邦第一砲兵團三個連駐於霍爾敦。戰鬥方面，一八三八年十二月三十一日卡里布一役無人陣亡，僅有伐木工被黑熊所傷，雙方正式部隊始終未曾交火；民兵因寒冷與疾病死亡的數十人，是這場衝突為數不多的部隊損失。最終一八四二年八月九日《韋伯斯特—阿什伯頓條約》把七千零一十五平方英里劃給美國、五千零一十二平方英里劃給英國，聯邦另向緬因州與麻薩諸塞州各付十五萬美元。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The dispute began with the Treaty of Paris of 1783, which did not settle the northern boundary; the joint commission of 1798 resolved only the stretch from the Saint Croix River to the Chiputneticook Lakes. The king of the Netherlands, acting as arbitrator in 1831, awarded the United States 7,908 square miles and Britain 4,119; Britain accepted and Maine refused, and the treaty failed in the Senate. On money and authority, the Maine legislature voted 800,000 dollars, the federal government appropriated ten million dollars and authorised the President to call out the militia, Congress authorised a force of fifty thousand men during the recess, and Nova Scotia voted 100,000 dollars. On 24 January 1839 the Maine legislature authorised the Governor to send the land agent, the sheriff and a posse of volunteer militia; the column left Bangor on 8 February; on 15 February Major General Hodsdon was authorised to bring a thousand more volunteers; General Order No 7 was issued on 19 February; and on 26 February the militia companies reached the upper Aroostook and began Fort Fairfield. Congress debated the matter on 2 March; federal engineers began the permanent works at Fort Fairfield in April; the militia was recalled in May and June on Scott's advice and the ground handed to an armed civil posse; Fort Kent was begun in October. Four companies of the 11th Regiment of Foot came down from Quebec, and three companies of the US 1st Artillery Regiment stood at Houlton. On the fighting, the clash at Caribou on 31 December 1838 cost no lives, the injuries being those of a woodcutter mauled by a bear, and the two regular forces never met; the militiamen who died of cold and disease, several dozen of them, were among the few military losses of the whole affair. The settlement of 9 August 1842, the Webster-Ashburton Treaty, awarded 7,015 square miles to the United States and 5,012 to Britain, and the federal government paid Maine and Massachusetts 150,000 dollars each.
cause: 起因是邊界線從未被認真畫過。一七八三年《巴黎條約》只用一句話把美國的北界定在「從聖克魯瓦河到聖羅克斯河源頭的一條線」，測量委員會在一七九八年把線畫到奇普特內蒂庫湖便停下，剩下的湖以北部分只說是「沿經度四十九度線北上至高地」，而高地究竟在哪裡，雙方各執一詞；一八一二年戰爭中英軍曾佔據緬因東部八個月並試圖永久吞併，戰後和約重申舊界，一八二〇年緬因脫離麻薩諸塞獨立時，這條模糊的界線立刻變成州政府最關心的問題。日常爭執集中在木材：新不倫瑞克把聖約翰河上游的白木視為造船桅杆的來源，早期默許兩岸伐木工越界，一八三〇年代雙方開始互相控告，聖約翰城甚至倚賴這批越界木材撐起自己的商業；美方則大量發出土地憑照與伐木許可，並在爭議地做人口登記、記錄戶籍、承認教會與地方選舉，等於在對方地界上建立行政。往後的加壓也是雙向的：英方召回一八三一年的荷蘭仲裁裁決並提出新方案，美方拒絕；一八三六年緬因州做特別人口普查，代表格里利在阿魯斯圖克河上游被新不倫瑞克逮捕，總督哈維指責緬因州長受賄並致書華盛頓警告用兵，州長鄧拉普則以「外國勢力入侵」發布總動員令，雙方的官方往來從領土爭議變成對主權與賄賂的指控，衝突便再無退路。
causeEn: The cause is that the boundary was never properly drawn. The Treaty of Paris of 1783 defined the northern limit of the United States in a single sentence, from the Saint Croix River to the headwaters of the Saint Croix, and the commission of 1798 carried the line as far as the Chiputneticook Lakes and then stopped, leaving everything north of the lakes to be described only as a line running north along the high ground that separates the waters of the Saint Lawrence from those draining south; where those highlands lay, each side asserted its own answer. British troops occupied eastern Maine for eight months during the War of 1812 with a view to annexing it permanently, and the restored peace repeated the old wording; when Maine separated from Massachusetts in 1820, that vague line became the new state's most pressing concern. The daily friction was about timber: New Brunswick valued the white pine of the upper Saint John as mast timber and had long turned a blind eye to cutters crossing the line, but by the 1830s each side was prosecuting the other, and the city of Saint John had come to depend on the trade. The Americans responded with land deeds, timber permits, censuses, registrations of births and marriages, and the organisation of a town under Maine law within the disputed country, that is, with an administration set up on British ground. After that the pressure ran both ways. Britain withdrew its acceptance of the Dutch arbitration of 1831 and offered a new line, which the Americans rejected; in 1836 Maine took a special census and its representative Greeley was arrested in the upper Aroostook; Governor Harvey accused the Governor of Maine of bribery and wrote to Washington threatening military action; Governor Dunlap answered with a general order announcing an invasion by a foreign power. The official correspondence had shifted from a dispute about land to an accusation about sovereignty and bribery, and from that point there was no way back.
impact: 後果是雙方的邊界問題被長期凍結在「未決」狀態，直到一八四二年才用一次外交交易收掉。過程中留下的制度先例影響甚遠：州民兵在聯邦拒絕出兵時自行組團邊界，聯邦最後仍以賠償州政府的名義結案，等於承認州在邊境問題上可以單方面行動；英國方面則在阿魯斯圖克河兩側建起福爾特菲爾德與福爾特肯特兩座要塞，兩地後來在美國內戰期間再次成為聯邦軍的據點，被沿用為北方對英國系統的哨所。一八四二年條約給美國多數爭議土地，但把北面一條通往哈利法克斯的陸路走廊留給英國，維持了加拿大與海事殖民地之間的冬季陸路聯絡，這條通道在後來修成鐵路，直到今日仍是英屬北美交通的骨幹，加拿大輿論因此長期把該條約視為英國方面的退讓。名稱上的諷刺也被保留下來：民間把這場衝突叫做「豬肉與豆子戰爭」或「馬達瓦斯卡戰爭」，說明它在多數人心中從來不是一場戰爭，而是一場行政僵局。它也留下了一段關於戰爭權力的教訓：兩個武裝團體可以在同一條河流的兩岸互相扣人、把軍隊開到對方的營地前面，卻沒有任何一方真正想打，最後靠的是英國公使與美國國務卿之間的一紙協議，而不是任何一場會戰。
impactEn: The consequence was that the boundary question on both sides remained frozen in an undecided state until it was settled by a diplomatic transaction in 1842. The institutional precedents left behind matter more than the land. The state militia had mustered on its own when the federal government refused to act, and the federal government eventually closed the matter by compensating the states, which amounted to accepting that a state might act on its own initiative along a frontier. On the British side the two forts at Fairfield and Kent were built on either side of the Aroostook, and both were used again by United States troops during the American Civil War, becoming outposts of the northern side of the old Atlantic frontier system. The treaty of 1842 gave the Americans most of the disputed ground but left the British a corridor to the north, the Halifax Road, keeping the overland winter link between Canada and the Maritime colonies, a route that was later paved into a railway and remains the backbone of transport in British North America to this day; Canadian opinion long treated the treaty as a British concession. The irony was kept in the name: popular usage called the affair the Pork and Beans War or the Madawaska War, which says that in the mind of most people it was never a war but an administrative deadlock. It also left a lesson about the conduct of war: two armed bodies could detain each other's men, bring troops to the front of the other's camp on the same river, and yet neither really wanted to fight, and the matter was closed by a treaty between a British envoy and a United States secretary of state rather than by any engagement.
result: 結果是沒有戰爭，卻有了條約。兩軍對峙三年之後，一八四二年八月九日《韋伯斯特—阿什伯頓條約》在華盛頓簽訂，爭議地約七千零一十五平方英里歸美國，五千零一十二平方英里歸英國，哈利法克斯公路的通行權留在英方，聯邦另向緬因州與麻薩諸塞州各付十五萬美元作為土地與費用補償；英國同時處理了與新罕布什爾、密西根、明尼蘇達的零星界線問題。戰場上的收尾則是行政性的：一八三九年五月與六月，緬因民兵依斯科特的建議撤回，武裝民事團接替佔據爭議地，聯邦工程兵建成的兩座要塞由正規軍駐守，新不倫瑞克則在對岸維持常設哨所，這種沿線對峙的格局一直維持到十九世紀末，兩國邊界從此以要塞與巡邏隊代替戰爭。戰爭的實際代價極小：正式部隊從未交火，傷亡主要是民兵在北方冬季行軍與駐紮中因寒冷與疾病折損的人數，以及卡里布衝突中因誤會引發的零星槍響。真正被解決的不是武器問題，而是主權問題的處理方式：英國最終接受由英美雙方代表直接劃界、並以一次性賠償換取雙方接受的做法，這套做法後來在美國對英的多次談判中被反覆採用。
resultEn: The result was no war, but a treaty. After three years of confrontation the Webster-Ashburton Treaty was signed at Washington on 9 August 1842: about 7,015 square miles of the disputed country went to the United States and 5,012 to Britain, the right of way for the Halifax Road stayed on the British side, and the federal government paid Maine and Massachusetts 150,000 dollars each for the land and the expenses of the period; Britain settled a number of minor boundary questions with New Hampshire, Michigan and Minnesota at the same time. The closing of the military phase was administrative rather than operational: in May and June 1839 the Maine militia was recalled on Scott's advice, the armed civil posse took over the disputed ground, and the two forts built by federal engineers were garrisoned by regular troops while New Brunswick kept permanent posts on the far bank, a pattern of facing pickets that lasted to the end of the century, with forts and patrols taking the place of war along the line. The cost of the affair was very small: the regular forces never met, and the losses were mostly militiamen worn down by cold and disease during the winter marches and camps in the north, together with the stray shots exchanged at Caribou. What was actually settled was not a question of weapons but a way of handling sovereignty: Britain finally accepted a line drawn directly by British and American commissioners, and bought acceptance on both sides with a single indemnity, a practice that was repeated in later American negotiations with Britain.
